EZZI BUILDING SERVICES PTY LTD
PERTH WESTERN AUSTRALIA 6036
EMPLOYMENT TYPE: FULL-TIME PERMANENT
SALARY: AUD $80,000 TO $100,000 PER ANNUM

Ezzi Building Services Pty Ltd is seeking suitably qualified and experienced applicants for the positions of Construction Project Manager and Project Builder in Perth, Western Australia. The successful applicant will be responsible for managing residential and/or commercial construction projects from planning through to completion, ensuring projects are delivered safely, on time, within budget and to a high standard of workmanship.

Responsibilities
The successful applicant will be responsible for overseeing construction projects, coordinating labour and subcontractors, liaising with clients, suppliers and consultants, and ensuring compliance with Australian building standards, workplace health and safety
requirements and company procedures.
The role requires strong project management capability, practical building knowledge and the ability to supervise works across multiple stages of construction.

Tasks
Key tasks include:
• Planning, coordinating and managing construction projects from commencement to completion.
• Preparing and reviewing project schedules and project plans, construction programs, budgets and work plans.
• Supervising site activities and coordinating trades, subcontractors and suppliers.
• Monitoring project progress, costs, materials, labour and quality of work.
• Interpreting plans, drawings, specifications and building documentation.
• Liaising with clients, architects, engineers, certifiers, local authorities and other stakeholders.
• Ensuring all work complies with relevant building codes, Australian standards, safety regulations and contractual requirements.
• Managing variations, delays, defects, site issues and project reporting.
• Conducting site inspections and ensuring quality control throughout the construction process.
• Maintaining accurate project records, reports, schedules and compliance documentation.

Skills
Applicants should have:
• Strong knowledge of construction methods, project delivery and site management.
• Excellent organisational, planning and time-management skills.
• Ability to manage budgets, timelines, subcontractors and construction resources.
• Sound understanding of workplace health and safety requirements.
• Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, plans and specifications.
• Strong communication and negotiation skills.
• Problem-solving ability and attention to detail.
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
• Proficiency with construction project management systems, scheduling tools and Microsoft Office or similar software.

Qualifications
Applicants must hold relevant qualifications in building, construction management, project management, civil construction, or a related field.
Relevant Australian or overseas qualifications may be considered, including a diploma, advanced diploma, bachelor degree or equivalent trade/background experience in the building and construction industry.

Experience
Applicants must have relevant experience in construction project management, building supervision or project delivery, if a bachelor's degree is present. If no degree, then at least 5 years of experience in the relevant industry.
Previous experience in residential, commercial or mixed-use construction projects will be highly regarded. Experience managing subcontractors, construction schedules, budgets, compliance requirements and client communications is essential.
Ezzi Building Services Pty Ltd is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from suitably qualified candidates.

About us:

Solid Home Solutions is your go-to expert for residential and commercial maintenance in Alice Springs, NT. Specializing in carpentry, painting, gyprock, fencing, and air-condition installation, we cater to both local and remote communities. Our experienced team is dedicated to providing top-notch service to ensure your property is in top shape.

As a key member of the Solid Home Solutions team, you will work directly alongside our Site Supervisor to deliver high-quality plastering and gyprock services for residential and commercial properties across Alice Springs and remote NT communities. In this role, you’ll be responsible for surface preparation, installing and finishing plasterboard, applying plaster and render, and ensuring all wall and ceiling surfaces are smooth, durable, and finished to our exacting standards—on time and to specification. result.description:
Full-time Wall and Floor Tiler position available with a competitive salary. Work in a dynamic team in Hurlstone Park, NSW 2193

•	Full-Time Position
•	$80,000 - $90,000 plus superannuation 
•	Operate within a professional setting.

FerMax Stone Pty Ltd is an Australian company established in 2012, specialising in the installation of premium wall and floor tiling, natural stone, porcelain and other high-quality surface finishes for residential and commercial projects. Since its establishment, the company has built a reputation for delivering quality workmanship, reliability and exceptional customer service across a wide range of projects.
On behalf of our client, we are looking for an experienced and skilled Wall and Floor tiler to join our team on a full-time basis

Position Responsibilities and Tasks

As a Wall and Floor Tiler, your duties will include, but will not be limited to:

•	Interpret plans and specifications; confirm measurements, quantities, layout lines and levels prior to commencing tiling works.
•	Measure, mark and set out surfaces using levelling equipment (including laser levels) to establish correct alignment, falls and datum lines.
•	Measure, cut, shape and install custom heritage mosaic tiles and decorative stone finishes, ensuring accurate pattern alignment, preserving heritage design features and delivering high-quality workmanship in accordance with project specifications.
•	Prepare wall and floor substrates by removing old tiles, grout and adhesives; filling holes and cracks; and cleaning/priming surfaces to ensure suitable adhesion and finish.
•	Lay and fix tiles (including ceramic, clay, slate, marble, glass and similar materials) to internal and external walls and floors to achieve required patterns, alignment and tolerances.
•	Apply adhesives and bedding materials to substrates and/or tile backs as required, ensuring correct coverage, bonding and curing in line with product specifications.
•	Cut, shape and fit tiles using hand and power tile-cutting tools to finish edges, corners and penetrations around fittings, pipes and fixtures.
•	Maintain consistent alignment and spacing throughout installation, checking for lippage, level, line and falls, and adjusting as required during installation.
•	Complete grouting, finishing and clean-down, including removing excess grout and presenting a consistent, defect-free surface finish.
•	Support waterproofing outcomes by assisting with waterproofing preparation/detailing and coordinating tiling works with waterproofing stages and inspection hold points, ensuring correct detailing at junctions and penetrations in wet areas and external areas.
•	Undertake substrate preparation activities that support tiling quality (e.g., grinding, levelling and surface preparation), and coordinate transitions/interfaces with epoxy or other protective floor finishes where required by project scope.
•	Work collaboratively on major construction sites across Sydney/NSW, liaising with site foremen and project managers regarding sequencing, access, quality inspections and program timeframes.
•	Maintain compliance with WHS requirements, including safe manual handling, correct PPE use, silica dust controls and safe operation of plant and tools used for cutting and surface preparation.


Qualifications and Skills:

•	Certificate III in Wall and Floor Tiling or relevant trade qualification.
•	At least two years of relevant experience.
•	Sound knowledge of wall and floor tiling techniques and installation methods.
•	Experience working with ceramic, porcelain, marble, granite and natural stone products.
•	Ability to read and interpret plans and technical drawings.
•	Strong attention to detail and commitment to high-quality workmanship.

Salary:
The role offers a remuneration package of $80,000 - $90,000 per annum, plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

How to Apply: 11 Recruitment is your pathway to securing this exciting opportunity. We are looking forward to facilitating your application and potentially welcoming you to a company that values expertise. Apply now and let us help you take the next step in your career.

CAMA0033

The Client
Melbourne Earthescapes Pty Ltd is a family-owned earthmoving, landscaping, and construction business based in Ravenhall, VIC, delivering landscaping, retaining wall construction, rockwork, stone installation, and transportation services across Melbourne and surrounding regions. 

They are seeking an experienced Stonemason to join their team in Ravenhall, VIC.

The Role
The Stonemason is responsible for constructing, repairing, and installing stone structures, retaining walls, masonry features, and related stonework in accordance with project specifications and construction requirements.
This is a full-time position with an annual salary of $80,000 to $90,000 plus superannuation. 

The Responsibilities
•	Cut and shape hard and soft stone blocks and masonry slabs to construct and renovate stone structures, kitchen benchtops, and monumental masonry
•	Lay pre-cut stones and masonry blocks in mortar to construct and repair walls, partitions, arches, and structural stone features
•	Study plans and specifications to determine material requirements, dimensions, and installation procedures
•	Erect and dismantle restricted height scaffolding in accordance with workplace safety procedures
•	Seal foundations with damp-resistant materials and apply mortar layers to support masonry installation works
•	Lay stones in rows, designs, and patterns while maintaining structural alignment and finish quality
•	Embed stone blocks in mortar and remove excess material to achieve clean and accurate finishes
•	Check vertical and horizontal alignment of stone structures using levelling and measuring equipment
•	Cut, shape, polish, and finish stone materials using hand tools, polishing equipment, and masonry machinery
•	Repair and maintain stone, brick, and masonry structures in accordance with construction requirements
•	Design, cut, and install monumental masonry and stone lettering works
•	Construct retaining walls, stone facades, and structural masonry installations for residential and commercial projects Choose and prepare appropriate metal materials for fabrication

The Requirements
•	Certificate III in Stonemasonry, Bricklaying, Construction, or equivalent trade qualification
•	Minimum 5 years’ experience as a Stonemason within construction, landscaping, or masonry environments
•	Minimum 5 years’ experience interpreting technical drawings, specifications, and construction measurements for masonry works
•	At least 5 years’ experience constructing retaining walls, stone structures, and masonry installations across residential or commercial projects
•	At least 5 years’ experience operating masonry tools, polishing equipment, cutting machinery, and stone fabrication tools
•	At least 5 years’ experience constructing stone retaining walls, rock walls, garden walls, paving, steps and outdoor stone features
•	Minimum 5 years’ experience using stone cutting, grinding, drilling, shaping and finishing tools in a construction or landscaping environment
•	Strong knowledge of masonry construction methods, mortar application, and stone finishing techniques
•	Ability to read and interpret technical plans, site measurements, and installation specifications accurately
•	Strong understanding of workplace safety procedures, scaffolding requirements, and construction compliance standards
•	White Card required
•	Excavator and Skid Steer licences preferred
•	Ability to work outdoors, at heights, and across varying construction site environments
•	Strong work ethic, reliability, and ability to work independently or within construction teams
•	High attention to detail and commitment to workmanship quality

Your new company     An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Infrastructure Engineer to join a well-established technology services organisation with a growing presence in Tasmania.  Based in Hobart, this permanent role will see you supporting and improving enterprise Linux and cloud environments that underpin critical services across the state. Working closely with both local and national engineering teams, you'll play a key role in maintaining platform stability, security and operational excellence in mission-critical environments where availability and reliability are paramount.    Your new role     As an Infrastructure Engineer, you will be responsible for administering and supporting Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) environments, ensuring systems remain secure, available and performing at their best. You will manage patching and upgrades, monitor infrastructure health, respond to incidents, and contribute to ongoing platform improvement initiatives.  Working across Azure and AWS environments, you'll help strengthen infrastructure resilience, support security and compliance requirements, and participate in a 24/7 on-call roster. You'll take ownership of critical incidents from identification through to resolution, applying strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills while working within established change management and governance frameworks. You'll also be responsible for conducting root cause analysis and maintaining operational documentation and standards.    What you'll need to succeed   
 
 Mandatory RHCE (Red Hat Certified Engineer) certification 
 Strong experience administering enterprise Linux/RHEL environments 
 Infrastructure engineering experience within enterprise or managed services environments 
 Experience supporting Azure and/or AWS platforms 
 Strong troubleshooting, incident management and problem-solving skills 
 Experience with patching, upgrades, system hardening and vulnerability remediation 
 Strong communication skills and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively 
 The ability to pass a mandatory police check 
 
 Highly regarded: 
 
 Experience within utilities, critical infrastructure, OT environments or managed services 
 
  What you'll get in return     You'll join a growing Hobart engineering team backed by experienced national engineering resources across Australia. In return, you'll gain exposure to enterprise scale Linux and cloud environments, enjoy flexible hybrid working arrangements, receive an on-call allowance, and have the opportunity to further develop your career within a collaborative and technically focused organisation that values accountability, continuous improvement and technical excellence.   What you need to do now

Please send to:  Victor.le@hays.com.au    If this job isn't exactly what you're looking for, but you're seeking a new position, please contact us for a private conversation about your career. result.description:
AKJ Services is a 100% Larrakia female owned, managed and controlled civil construction company. We deliver across three streams: Civil, Development and Defence.

Established in 2018, AKJ Services has grown a strong reputation for successful project delivery and capable project management. Our relationship contracting approach is nuanced by our Larrakia cultural protocols and social impact benefits across employment and supply chain opportunities.

We are seeking to employ experienced Mechanical Technician to join our team of dedicated professionals. We are looking for hardworking individuals who can meet company challenges and surpass client expectations.

The Mechanical Technician is responsible for ensuring the optimal performance, safety, and reliability of vehicles and equipment through expert maintenance, diagnostics, and repair.

Key duties include but are not limited to:
Perform regular scheduled preventive maintenance service on a range of vehicles and mechanical equipment to ensure operational efficiency and longevity
Identify, assess, and troubleshoot mechanical issues using computerised diagnostic systems
Dismantle, repair, and replace worn or defective mechanical parts, referencing service manuals and technical documentation as needed
Design and implement proactive mechanical maintenance strategies to minimise downtime and prevent costly vehicle or equipment breakdowns
Diagnose and resolve mechanical malfunctions, ensuring timely and effective repairs
Conduct post-repair testing and adjustments to verify proper performance and compliance with safety standards
Accurately complete and maintain service records, inspection reports, and compliance documentation in accordance with regulatory requirements
May perform vehicle inspections and issue roadworthiness certificates or provide detailed recommendations to meet legal and safety standards
May attend to on-site vehicle or equipment breakdowns, providing prompt diagnostic and repair services
Keep the workshop clean and organised while strictly adhering to health, safety, and environmental regulations

To be considered for this role, you must have:
Mechanical Technician trade qualification or equivalent
Strong mechanical knowledge on a wide variety of vehicle and equipment
Ability to work well both independently and in a team environment
Strong communication skills
Strong diagnostic abilities
Self-motivated, organised, punctual and reliable
Must have great work ethics

If you meet the above criteria and would like to be considered for this position, please apply now!

Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

Diesel Motor Mechanic
Coath Rd, West Kalgoorlie WA 6430
Ful-time

Our client, VPT Mechanical Solutions, is seeking experienced Diesel Motor Mechanics to join their growing team in West Kalgoorlie, Western Australia. As part of the VPT Group, a leading Western Australian industrial services company supporting mining and resource operations, they deliver mechanical, fire suppression, and drilling support services with a strong focus on safety, reliability, quality, and operational excellence.

This is an excellent opportunity for qualified Diesel Motor Mechanics who are looking to build a long-term career within a supportive and professional environment.

Key Responsibilities

* Diagnose and rectify mechanical and electrical faults in diesel engines, heavy vehicles, and mobile equipment.
* Dismantle, inspect, repair, and reassemble engines, transmissions, steering systems, suspension, braking systems, and other mechanical components.
* Replace worn or defective parts in accordance with manufacturer specifications and service manuals.
* Perform routine servicing and preventative maintenance, including oil changes, lubrication, engine tune-ups, and scheduled inspections.
* Test and adjust repaired components to ensure safe and efficient operation.
* Use computer-based diagnostic equipment to identify faults and assess engine performance.
* Inspect vehicles and equipment for roadworthiness and compliance, recommending repairs where required.
* Attend breakdowns and provide on-site mechanical support when necessary.
* Maintain accurate service records while adhering to workplace health and safety procedures.

Skills and Qualifications

* Relevant trade qualification in Diesel Mechanics or an equivalent automotive mechanical trade.
* **Minimum of three (3) years of relevant full-time experience** as a Diesel Motor Mechanic.
* Strong diagnostic, troubleshooting, and problem-solving abilities.
* Experience working with diesel engines, heavy vehicles, and mining or industrial equipment is highly regarded.
* Sound understanding of workplace health and safety requirements.
* Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team.
* Relevant licences and certifications will be advantageous.

What Our Client Offers

* Competitive annual salary of AUD $90,000 – $100,000, depending on qualifications and experience.
* Full-time, long-term employment opportunity.
* Supportive and safety-focused workplace culture.
* Ongoing training and career development opportunities.
* Opportunity to work with a respected Western Australian industrial services company supporting the mining and resources sector.
